text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** Several of the guides below say it is the standard for new power stations, and NMC mostly survives in older, compact or clearance units.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC (one guide says up to 2,000). At one cycle a day, that is about 8-11 years versus under 2-3 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and slower when they failed. One test peaked at 259 °C for LFP versus 731 °C for NMC. LFP isn't fireproof, and in one overcharge test it reached thermal runaway sooner, but its failures were milder. That matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Cost over time:** The upfront price gap has largely closed. One guide puts median price per Wh at $0.55 for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC. LFP costs far less per rated cycle ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kg. But in finished stations the gap is small, about 10-16% per pound in two databases. The inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way, and some LFP stations weigh less per Wh than some NMC ones ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Things that don't differ much**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations of either chemistry refuse to charge below 32°F. Check the specific model's manual ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cycle ratings:** They aren't directly comparable across brands. Check the end point (80% vs 70%) and the test conditions.

**How to decide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, off-grid, solar):** Choose LiFePO4.
- **Occasional use (a few outages a year, some weekend trips):** Either works, because calendar aging will limit the battery before cycles do. Choose on weight and price.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.
- **Older NMC unit at an LFP price:** Look twice before buying.

**An LFP example:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter and a 6,000+ cycle rating (to 80%).
